I work on bushfire hazard assessment with UNSW Bushfire. My background is in
computational fluid dynamics: simulating turbulent flows on high performance
computing clusters, first for heat transfer over rough surfaces and then for
the ember storms that drive house loss in bushfires.

My Ph.D. research at UNSW Canberra is on computational modelling of ember
storms at the wildland-urban interface, using large-eddy simulation with
Lagrangian particles. Before that I completed an M.Phil. in Mechanical
Engineering at The University of Melbourne (2021, First Class Honours), where
I used direct numerical simulation to study momentum and heat transfer in
rough-wall turbulent flows. I graduated *magna cum laude* from Temple
University with a B.S. in Mechanical Engineering in 2018.

## Interests

Bushfire modelling · computational fluid dynamics · large-eddy simulation ·
spectral element method · high performance computing
